champion: Breast Cancer with Axillary Lymph Node Metastasis
ordered_diagnoses: Breast Cancer with Axillary Lymph Node Metastasis
Infiltrative Ductal Carcinoma of the Breast

facts.raw_span: A 48-year-old woman
type 2 diabetes
hypertension
bilateral breast lumps of one-week duration
no family history of breast or ovarian cancer
a 4 × 4 cm hard lump in the lower inner quadrant fixed to the chest wall
MRI showed a 3.8 × 3.5 cm irregular spiculated mass in the left breast suspicious for malignancy
a 2.3 × 1.5 cm well-defined lesion in the right breast with a type 1 contrast enhancement pattern (< 6% probability of malignancy)
bilateral axillary lymphadenopathy
poorly cohesive clusters of ductal cells with pleomorphism, hyperchromasia, and prominent nucleoli
infiltrative duct cell carcinoma that was estrogen- and progesterone-receptor positive
FNAC of the left axillary lymph node showed similar malignant cells

concepts.preferred_label: Infiltrative Ductal Carcinoma of the Breast
concepts.why: The patient has a 3.8 × 3.5 cm irregular spiculated mass in the left breast suspicious for malignancy, and FNAC results show poorly cohesive clusters of ductal cells with pleomorphism, hyperchromasia, and prominent nucleoli.
The patient has a 2.3 × 1.5 cm well-defined lesion in the right breast with a type 1 contrast enhancement pattern, which is suggestive of a fibroadenoma.
The patient has type 2 diabetes, which is a known endocrine disorder.
The patient has hypertension, which is a known cardiovascular disease.
The patient has bilateral axillary lymphadenopathy, which is a known symptom of breast cancer.

aliases: Breast Cancer with Lymph Node Involvement
concepts.preferred_label: Breast Cancer with Axillary Lymph Node Metastasis
concepts.why: The patient has FNAC results showing similar malignant cells in the left axillary lymph node, which is indicative of breast cancer with lymph node metastasis.
The patient has infiltrative ductal carcinoma that is estrogen-receptor positive, which is a known subtype of breast cancer.
The patient has infiltrative ductal carcinoma that is progesterone-receptor positive, which is a known subtype of breast cancer.

rationales.F02: Type 2 diabetes is a known comorbidity, but not directly related to breast cancer.
rationales.F03: Hypertension is a known comorbidity, but not directly related to breast cancer.
rationales.F06: A hard lump fixed to the chest wall is highly suggestive of malignancy.
rationales.F07: MRI showing a spiculated mass is highly suggestive of malignancy.
rationales.F10: Cytology showing poorly cohesive clusters of ductal cells with pleomorphism is highly suggestive of malignancy.
rationales.F11: Infiltrative duct cell carcinoma with estrogen and progesterone receptor positivity is a specific diagnosis.
rationales.F12: FNAC of the left axillary lymph node showing similar malignant cells confirms metastasis.
